ai.description: *Micrixalus specca* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring distinct light spots. It is identified by its slender body, rounded snout, and characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus specca* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of distinct, small white or yellowish spots scattered across its dark brown dorsum, unlike its unspotted congeners.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus specca* inhabits the moist evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky, shaded streams at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male *Micrixalus specca* perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, rhythmically extending and waving their hind legs against the backdrop of flowing water.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus specca* is an egg-laying frog that breeds during the monsoon. It lays small clutches of eggs in stream-bed crevices, which are then covered with gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus specca* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Spotted Dancing Frog produces a high-pitched, short "tink" sound, often heard as a rapid, repetitive series near fast-flowing, rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
